fixtures.label: Open-item floor — 4 columns, and the population rule
fixtures.description: The `open_item` FORMAT and the 4-column FLOOR. Its partner is `balance-forward-subtree`, which covers the other format. ⚠️ `format` is a stored POPULATION rule, not a template param, so the two states come from two captured DOCUMENTS and neither can be re-rendered from the other — and NOTHING mechanical enforces the pair: `lint:fixtures` check 5 only fires on declared boolean params, and check 4 is per-fixture parity, which one fixture and one golden satisfy. This family passes every check with either one deleted. Neither is a near-duplicate; each is the only golden over half the template. Four jobs. (1) THE FLOOR — one account, no line carries a `reference`, and the running Balance column is absent by design on an open-item statement, so every conditional is off and the header is exactly Details / Date / Charges / Payments. The partner is the 7-column ceiling. (2) THE POPULATION RULE — `open_item` prints only invoices whose REPLAYED balance is non-zero and takes no date bound: `buildOrgStatement` refuses a `from_date`, and `to_date` defaults to UNBOUNDED so a post-dated invoice still shows. The narrowing cannot move the closing balance (a settled invoice contributes +total and −total to one sum), which is what makes it exact rather than a summary. (3) THE PAYMENTS COLUMN IS NOT DEAD — invoice 2364 is partly settled, so a real settlement line lands in it. The column is UNCONDITIONAL (a statement shows both sides of the ledger; a blank cell reads as zero, not as missing data), so without a settled line here it would be frozen empty by every golden in the family. (4) A THREE-NODE CHAIN SCOPED AT THE LEAF — every line's frozen chain matches the scope, so the Account column correctly does NOT appear; the partner proves it appears when lines genuinely span accounts. Captured from prod org `Enemies Movie, LLC / (default) / Locations` — the smallest multi-invoice open-item account available (2363, 2371, 2364).
